pictures.scene: Jan de Bray, The Regents of the Guild of Saint Luke — three men in black gowns with broad white falling collars grouped round a table spread with a red Turkish carpet, a heavy-faced man at the left holding up an engraved gold medal, a long-haired man standing behind him with a silver tassel in his hand, a third leaning his cheek on his fist at the right while another hand points to a drawing lying on the table, gilt picture frames on the panelled wall behind, then the pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from jerusalem gathered around jesus, and they saw some of his disciples eating with hands that were defiled, that is, unwashed
pictures.name: pd_de_bray_regenten_sint_lucasgilde

pictures.scene: Velazquez, An Old Woman Cooking Eggs — an old woman in a white headcloth and a russet bodice turning her head in profile as she lifts a wooden spoon over a red earthenware pan of eggs set on a clay brazier, another egg held ready in her left hand, a boy at the left carrying a glass flask and a melon, a brass mortar and pestle, a white glazed dish with a knife laid across it and a straw basket hanging on the wall above, now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the pharisees and all the jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially, and on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash, and there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining
pictures.name: pd_velazquez_an_old_woman_cooking_eggs

pictures.scene: Dirck van Delen, The Pharisee and the Publican — a tall white church interior of clustered columns and ribbed vaults standing over a blue and cream chequered floor, the Pharisee at the left in a plum cloak with his hand raised and his chin lifted as he prays, the publican far off at the right in a red mantle with his head bowed and both hands crossed on his breast, so the pharisees and scribes questioned jesus, why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders, instead, they eat with defiled hands, jesus answered them, isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written, these people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me
pictures.name: pd_delen_pharisee_and_publican

pictures.scene: Max Liebermann, Jesus in the Temple — the boy Christ in a pale belted robe and sandals standing in a crowded temple hall with His hands raised as He speaks, grey-bearded scholars in white prayer shawls and long black coats leaning in close around Him, one of them with his hand at his mouth, more men standing at reading desks in the shadow behind, a worn stone-flagged floor underfoot, they worship me in vain, they teach as doctrine the precepts of men, you have disregarded the commandment of god to keep the tradition of men
pictures.name: pd_liebermann_jesus_im_tempel

pictures.scene: Philippe de Champaigne, Moses Presenting the Tablets of the Law — Moses in a blue mantle over a gold-embroidered breastplate holding up the two stone tablets with both hands, his white beard spread over his chest and two horns of light in his hair, the lettered commandments legible down the stone with the charge to honor your father and your mother among them, a gilt rod lying across his arm, a plain dark ground behind him, he went on to say, you neatly set aside the command of god to maintain your own tradition, for moses said, honor your father and your mother, and anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death
pictures.name: pd_de_champaigne_moses_presenting_the_tablets_of_the_law

pictures.scene: Quentin Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a moneylender in a black fur-trimmed cap weighing coins in a small hand balance over a table strewn with gold pieces, rings and pearls, his wife beside him in a scarlet gown and a white coif turning her eyes away from the illuminated book under her fingers, a convex mirror standing on the table edge, a shelf of ledgers, a glass flask and an apple on the panelled wall behind, but you say that if a man says to his father or mother, whatever you would have received from me is corban, that is, a gift devoted to god, he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching at Athens — Paul standing barefoot on a stone step in a green tunic and a rose mantle with both arms flung up as he speaks, listeners seated and crouching on the steps around him, a man in a red cap leaning back to stare up at him, a curly-headed youth and a group in gold and blue drapery pressing in at the right, heavy classical arches and columns rising behind, thus you nullify the word of god by the tradition you have handed down, and you do so in many such matters, once again jesus called the crowd to him and said, all of you, listen to me and understand
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_paul_preaching_at_athens

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Supper at Emmaus — Christ seated at a white-clothed table in a red robe under a pale mantle with His hand stretched out in blessing and His eyes lowered, a roast fowl on a majolica dish before Him, a torn loaf, a glass of red wine and a basket of grapes, pomegranates and pears tipped out to the very edge of the table, an old disciple throwing up both hands at the right, a plain dim wall behind them, nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him, but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him, after jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, his disciples inquired about the parable
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_supper_at_emmaus

pictures.scene: Jan Steen, Prayer Before the Meal — a cottage interior lit by a leaded window, a young mother in a white cap and a grey jacket sitting with a baby in a blue frock on her lap and her head bent over her folded hands, a man opposite holding his hat against his chest with his eyes shut, a big crusty loaf and a round cheese on a white cloth between them, a platter of ham on a barrel draped with a fringed rug, a hoop of oak leaves with a bell hanging from the beam and a lettered verse board on the wall, are you still so dull, he asked, do you not understand, nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him, because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated, thus all foods are clean
pictures.name: pd_steen_prayer_before_the_meal

pictures.scene: Poussin, Christ and the Woman Taken in Adultery — Christ standing on the paved square in a blue tunic and a red mantle with one hand pointing down at the writing by His feet and His face turned toward the accusers, the woman sunk on the ground at the left in a white shift and a blue skirt with her head bowed and her eyes closed, a man carrying a child watching from behind, townsmen crowding in at the right with their hands spread, stone houses and a long flight of steps rising behind, he continued, what comes out of a man, that is what defiles him, for from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery
pictures.name: pd_poussin_christ_and_the_woman_taken_in_adultery

pictures.scene: Caravaggio, The Cardsharps — a boy in a black velvet doublet with a lace collar and lace cuffs studying the cards in his hands with his eyes lowered, an older man in a plumed hat leaning close over his shoulder to spy the hand, the young cheat at the right in a striped yellow and black doublet reaching behind his back for the hidden card, dice and a backgammon board lying on the red carpeted table, greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness, all these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_the_cardsharps

pictures.scene: Hendrick Sorgh, Market by the Harbour — a housewife in a red jacket and a long white apron holding a basket down at her side at the left, a man in a black hat and a grey cloak turning toward her with his hand out, a market woman in a scarlet jacket and a white collar passing a dish of greens across her stall, a child in a white cap looking up beside her, baskets of fish and heaps of carrots and cabbages in front, furled sails and a warehouse roof behind, jesus left that place and went to the region of tyre, not wanting anyone to know he was there, he entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice, instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit soon heard about jesus, and she came and fell at his feet
pictures.name: pd_sorgh_markt_am_hafen

pictures.scene: Benjamin Vautier, Children at the Table — an arm reaching in from the right to tip a ladle of porridge into the bowl a small boy in a green jacket holds up with both hands, four more children ranged along the white-clothed table with their bowls and spoons, a fair-haired girl perched on the bench with her arms at her sides, a barefoot boy in a straw hat crowding in behind her, hens pecking about the flagstones under the bench, now she was a greek woman of syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter, first let the children have their fill, he said, for it is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs
pictures.name: pd_vautier_kinder_am_tisch

pictures.scene: Frans Snyders, The Pantry — a shallow basket of pike, carp and eels set on the corner of a white-clothed table, bunches of white and red grapes and a peach heaped above them, a dead peacock hanging head downward over the edge, and a black and tan dog slipping in underneath with its nose lifted to the hanging cloth while a second dog bares its teeth at the left, yes, lord, she replied, even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs, then jesus told her, because of this answer, you may go, the demon has left your daughter
pictures.name: pd_snyders_pantry

pictures.scene: Gabriel Metsu, The Sick Child — a woman in a brown jacket with a wide white collar and a dark jewelled cap sitting with a listless child laid back across her lap, the child in a yellow jacket and a white shift leaning its head against her shoulder and staring out of the picture, the woman's blue apron and red skirt filling the foreground, a rolled map pinned to the pale wall behind her and a small dark framed Crucifixion hanging above, and she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone, then jesus left the region of tyre and went through sidon to the sea of galilee and into the region of the decapolis
pictures.name: pd_metsu_the_sick_child

pictures.scene: El Greco, Christ Healing the Blind — a bald bearded elder in a blue mantle stretching his arm right across the picture to point toward the healing, three more heads crowded shoulder to shoulder behind him and a fair young man looking over them, a woman in a rose bodice and a gold skirt turned away at the right, a white classical temple and a wagon drawn by horses on the paved square beyond, piled grey cloud filling the sky above, some people brought to him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged jesus to place his hand on him, so jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put his fingers into the man's ears, then he spit and touched the man's tongue
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_christ_healing_the_blind

pictures.scene: Eugene Burnand, The High Priestly Prayer — Christ standing in a plain white robe with His arms spread wide and His face lifted, His eyes raised to heaven as He prays, a dark-bearded disciple pressed close at His left in a grey cloak, another at His right covering his own face with his hand, a pale round arch rising behind their heads, and looking up to heaven, he sighed deeply and said to him, ephphatha, which means, be opened, immediately the man's ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly
pictures.name: pd_burnand_hogepriesterlijk_gebed

pictures.scene: Andrei Ryabushkin, A Moscow Street on a Holiday — a young woman in a scarlet coat buttoned with pearls and a white flowered kerchief walking the muddy plank road with a thin candle held in both hands, a roadside shrine with a gilded icon at the left, two men resting on a bench beside it, a bearded rider in a brocade coat and a tall black cap sitting a black horse behind her, log houses, a wooden watchtower and yellow birches under a dim sky, jesus ordered them not to tell anyone, but the more he ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it, the people were utterly astonished and said, he has done all things well, he makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak
pictures.name: pd_ryabushkin_moscow_street_holiday

lines.text: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus,
and they saw some of His disciples eating with hands that were defiled, that is, unwashed.
Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.
And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash. And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.
So the Pharisees and scribes questioned Jesus: Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.
Jesus answered them, Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites, as it is written: These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.
They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.
You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men.
He went on to say, You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition.
For Moses said, Honor your father and your mother, and Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.
But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, Whatever you would have received from me is Corban, that is, a gift devoted to God,
he is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.
Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down. And you do so in many such matters.
Once again Jesus called the crowd to Him and said, All of you, listen to Me and understand:
Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him; but the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.
After Jesus had left the crowd and gone into the house, His disciples inquired about the parable.
Are you still so dull? He asked. Do you not understand? Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,
because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated. Thus all foods are clean.
He continued: What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.
For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality, theft, murder, adultery,
greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.
All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.
Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre. Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house, but was unable to escape their notice.
Instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit soon heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.
Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin, and she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.
First let the children have their fill, He said. For it is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs.
Yes, Lord, she replied, even the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs.
Then Jesus told her, Because of this answer, you may go. The demon has left your daughter.
And she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone.
Then Jesus left the region of Tyre and went through Sidon to the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.
Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak, and they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.
So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd, and put His fingers into the man's ears. Then He spit and touched the man's tongue.
And looking up to heaven, He sighed deeply and said to him, Ephphatha! which means, Be opened!
Immediately the man's ears were opened and his tongue was released, and he began to speak plainly.
Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone. But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.
The people were utterly astonished and said, He has done all things well! He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!
